title: harness-profile.json
description: The one file that holds every value of a project's harness, each named by its role. The tools implement the subset of JSON Schema that this file uses (tools/lib/profile.mjs). A role without a value is left out of the generated profile document.

project.description: What the project is, for the profile document.

name.description: The short name of the project.

title.description: The display name of the project.

product.description: One sentence on what the project builds.

packages.description: The packages of the repository, in Markdown.

entryFile.description: The agent entry file and how it is loaded, in Markdown.

frameworkSource.description: Where the framework copy comes from, as one phrase for the profile document.

owner.description: Who owns the project and approves rule changes.

url.description: The web address of the repository.

host.description: The name of the repository host.

adapters.description: The adapters the project selected on the three axes (design §4).

stacks.description: One or more stack adapters: a name, or an object { "adapter": <name>, "packages": [<folder>, …] } with the folders (relative to the repository root) that the stack owns. A project with several stacks lists the folders of each, and two stacks must not claim the same folder (`harness check profile`).

items.description: A stack adapter name, or an object { "adapter": <name>, … }.

coverageGate.description: The coverage gate: the minimum, in percent, of each measure.

coveragePackages.description: The packages that carry a coverage gate.

quality.description: Prose roles of the quality gates, for the profile document.

coverageMechanism.description: What holds the coverage gate value and who reads it.

coverageScope.description: What the gate is applied to.

coverageScopeMechanism.description: The mechanism that applies the scope.

coverageExclusions.description: What is excluded from coverage and where each exclusion is justified.

localGateMechanism.description: The hook and script of the local gate.

requiredChecksMechanism.description: What sets the required checks on the host.

requiredChecks.description: The required checks: the names of the jobs that must pass before a merge.

requiredCheckNotes.description: A note per required check, for the profile document.

productionNote.description: A note on the production branch, for the profile document.

integrationNote.description: A note on the integration branch, for the profile document.

retention.description: The rule on keeping merged branches.

paths.description: Paths of the repository, relative to its root.

plan.description: The folder of the development plan.

phases.description: The folder of the phase files.

issues.description: The folder of the issue queue: defects and improvements found in use, one file per issue (`I-<n>.md`) with its log beside it, an index of the open ones, and `archived/` for the finished ones.

backlog.description: The folder of the backlog: the feature requests, which are not defects and are built only when the owner puts them into a release; one file per item (`B-<n>.md`) with its `Source:` (`report` with the link of each report, `owner` or `agent`), an index of the open ones, and `archived/` for the finished ones. Optional: a project without the role has no backlog.

offPlan.description: The folder of the off-plan record: work that no task covers (documentation, tooling, CI, a change of the plan) is recorded in a fragment of its own, one file per pull request named `<pull request number>-<slug>.md` (what changed, why and who asked, what it leaves to do), and an index `README.md` that says how a fragment reads. `harness plan log --off-plan` prints the fragments, and `harness check off-plan` lists the merged pull requests with neither a `Plan:` line nor a fragment, from the commit that added the index. Optional: a project without the role keeps no off-plan record.

releases.description: The file of the release order: one table `Release | Status | Tasks, in order | Consumers | Notes` (status ⬜ planned · 🟡 developing · 🏷 a development version cut · ✅ released · ⏭ skipped on purpose) and a list "Not scheduled", beside the plan index, which links to it and shows the current release in a generated block. The tools read the order of the tasks from its column of the tasks. Optional: a project that ships no versions has no such file, and a project without the role keeps its order as the section "Order of development" of the plan index.

flows.description: The folder of the flows: one file per flow (`flow-<n>-<slug>.md`, an ordered chain of steps that delivers one or more releases of the releases file, with a settings block that an orchestrator reads) and its append-only log beside it (`flow-<n>-<slug>.log.md`), and an index (`README.md`) that `harness plan summary` writes and the releases block of the plan index links. The procedure `run-flow` runs a flow. Optional, and only with `paths.releases`: a project without the role has no flows.

procedures.description: The folder of the project's own procedures, files of the format of `core/procedures/` (`<name>.md` with the frontmatter `name`, `description`, `invocation`). The skill generators and the procedures block of the entry file list them with the framework's; a name that the framework's procedures have too is an error. Optional: a project without the role has none.

profileDocument.description: Where the profile document is generated.

entryFile.description: The agent entry file: the CORE scan allows its one "Role binding" line to name the project's values.

frameworkDir.description: The folder that holds the framework's tools and core: `harness` in a project that uses the framework, `.` in the framework's own repository (lock mode self).

plan.description: Prose roles of the plan conventions, for the profile document.

taskId.description: The form of a task id.

phasesWithFragments.description: Which phases write a log fragment per task.

logCommand.description: The command that prints the implementation log.

resumePhrases.description: The phrases that resume a phase.

openEndedPhase.description: Deprecated since 0.2.0 (the issue queue, `paths.issues`, replaces the open-ended phase); kept so that a profile written before loads, and removed from it by the migration.

specificationCitation.description: How the product specification is cited.

complexity.description: The agent-complexity markers of the plan (design §3.4). Without this role the plan has no markers. With it, every open task of a phase file carries one in an `Agent` column before `SP` (done tasks are exempt), and the plan index shows each phase's range. A marker rates the reasoning a task needs, not its size.

scale.description: The markers and what each one means, from the lightest to the heaviest (the order of the keys).

models.description: The model and effort for each marker, which the session start prints for the next task (the default comes from the runtime adapter).

openEndedPhaseNumber.description: Deprecated since 0.2.0 (the issue queue, `paths.issues`, replaces the open-ended phase); kept so that a profile written before loads, and removed from it by the migration.

reports.description: Reports from users on the repository host (task 3.16): whether an agent takes them in, and whether a consuming project sends the defects it finds in the framework upstream. Both need a host adapter with the `reports` role; a host without it keeps both switches `off`. A local, ignored file, `harness-profile.local.json`, may override these three values at once without a pull request (for example `{ "reports": { "intake": "off" } }` pauses the intake when reports flood in).

intake.description: `off`: no hook line and no skill. `notify`: the session start prints the open reports and those not yet triaged, and the agent does not process them; the owner starts the triage. `auto`: the agent triages before other work, at most `triageLimit` reports a session, and the rest wait.

triageLimit.description: The most reports an agent triages in one session when `intake` is `auto` (1 or more).

upstream.description: For a consuming project: what it does with a defect of the framework that it suspects. `off`: it is noted in the task's log and the owner told, with no draft. `ask`: the agent searches the framework's reports for the same problem, drafts a report and posts it after the owner's approval. `post`: as `ask`, without the approval.

probes.description: How taking a version of the framework handles the cold-start probes of the project (report 65): each probe whose areas the version touched is a session of its own that reads thousands of words, for every release. A local, ignored file, `harness-profile.local.json`, may override `run` on one machine without a pull request.

run.description: `auto`: whoever takes the version runs the probes `harness probes` lists, each as a separate session, and reports what each read against the last review. `ask` (the default): the owner is asked first and the probes run only on a yes; where nobody can be asked it behaves as `disabled`. `disabled`: the probes are not run, and the output of `migrate` and `harness probes` only says how to run them. No command starts a probe itself yet, so `auto` and `ask` are instructions to the one who takes the version.

api.description: The public API, for projects that have one.

languages.description: The languages of the project, for projects that have several.

harness.description: The language of the harness and the design documents.

commands.description: The commands of the project, run from the repository root.

changedCoverage.description: The coverage of the changed files.

harnessSync.description: Take the framework again from its source.

harnessDiff.description: Show the local change of the vendored copy.

apiClient.description: Regenerate the client of the API.

dbUp.description: Start the local database. With `dbMigrate` and `dbSeed` it forms the optional database commands; the method's local-database step after a phase applies only where they are set.

dbMigrate.description: Apply migrations to the local database (an optional database command, with `dbUp`).

dbSeed.description: Seed the local database (an optional database command, with `dbUp`).

terms.description: The term lists of the harness review and the CORE scan: regular expressions, case-insensitive.

stack.description: Stack terms, which must not appear in CORE or DOMAIN text.

product.description: Product terms, which must not appear in CORE text.

productGeneric.description: Generic words of the product list, judged in context and not scanned.

projectValues.description: Project values, which must not appear in CORE text.

exceptions.description: Hits of the CORE scan in the vendored `core/` that the project accepts until its next sync: a leak it reported upstream and waits for the fix of. Each holds for one framework version only; after a sync to another version `harness check core` fails on it.

file.description: The file of the hit, as the scan prints it (for example `harness/core/method/method.md`).

report.description: The link to the report in the framework's repository.

version.description: The framework version (`version` of the lock) the exception holds for.

contexts.description: The bounded contexts of the product knowledge.

documents.description: The document map: the path of each document that the profile document links.

method.description: The engineering method; the entry file's rules link it.

riskRegister.description: The risk register (the plan method, section 4). Optional: the bootstrap writes the framework's template there once; a project that leaves it empty has no such file.

rfcs.description: The index of the design records (RFCs) with their template (the plan method, section 4). Optional: the bootstrap writes the framework's template there once, and the records sit in its folder; a project that leaves it empty has no such file.

layers.description: The layer map (design §8.2): globs per layer (`*` inside a folder, `**` across folders, a leading `!` removes). The tools add the vendored copy (CORE), the profile file, the lock, the profile document and the bindings (PROFILE), and the folder of a framework source (outside the map).

scope.description: The tracked files the map covers: each must be in exactly one layer.

excluded.description: Files in the scope that are outside the map (third-party files, for example).

core.description: The project's own CORE files, one per entry: a path, optionally followed by `sections` and the numbers of the sections that are CORE (the rest of the file belongs to another layer); the CORE scan reads them. A project that uses the framework needs none: the vendored copy and the entry file's managed rule blocks are CORE without an entry.

adapter.description: ADAPTER: what is specific to the stack, the runtime or the host.

profile.description: PROFILE files beyond the ones the tools know.

state.description: STATE: records that grow or are dated.

entry.description: ENTRY: the files an agent or a person reads first.

denyRead.description: Gitignore-style patterns of the paths an agent must not read (secrets only; files that merely cost context are not listed). A pattern with ! is a carve-out. The agent-runtime adapter turns them into its read exclusions, and `harness check scaffold` holds that they are there.

hooks.description: The project's part of the Git hooks.

prePushSetup.description: A shell file, relative to the root, that the pre-push hook sources before the gate runs: the local settings of the checkout (an `.env` file, the address of the database).

gate.description: The local gate of a push (`harness gate`, design §7.3): what the project adds to the plan of its stacks.

outside.description: Globs of the files that no check of the gate looks at (the CI configuration, the agent's settings).

isolated.description: Globs of the files that cannot change a package's code (scripts, documents, the vendored framework): they never trigger the full run of a stack, only the steps that name them.

needs.description: What the tests of some packages need before they run: a need (such as "database") and the packages whose test steps have it.

prepare.description: The module of the project that gets a need ready, per need: a Node module that exports prepare({ root, run }) and throws, with a message that says what to do, when the push must stop.

steps.description: The project's own steps: a label, the commands to run (each an argument list), the files that trigger it (`when`, default: any relevant change), the changes it is skipped for (`unlessOnly`), and paths that must not differ afterwards (`diff`, with a `hint` for the message).

host.description: What the repository host can do for this repository (design §4.3).

protection.description: Whether the host can enforce the protection of the production and the integration branch on this repository (a plan or visibility may rule it out). `harness host protect` detects the real answer and fails when it differs from this value.

autoMerge.description: Whether an agent enables the host's auto-merge on the pull requests it may merge without asking (the task and plan-related pull requests of a named phase), so that the host merges them once the required checks pass. Not set: on where `host.protection` is true, off where it is false (nothing would require the checks there). Off brings back the rule that an agent asks before it merges and never enables auto-merge unless asked.

checks.description: The checks of `harness check all` and of the push gate.

roleOnlyPaths.description: Globs of the files that name branches, the repository, plan paths and the coverage packages by role, never by value: scripts, hooks, workflows and the Markdown documents of the stack, operations and testing guides. `harness check values` fails on a value of the profile spelled out in them (Markdown: outside fenced code blocks).

documentationPaths.description: Globs of the files that count as documentation: a change of nothing else skips the code checks in CI and in the push gate (`harness ci changes`).

project.description: The project's own checks: commands that `harness check all` runs from the root after the framework's checks.

indexedFolders.description: Folders whose README.md is their index: it must link every file and subfolder of the folder that Git tracks, so a new document cannot be left out (`harness check links`). A subfolder named like a document belongs to that document.

productKnowledge.description: The product knowledge that `harness check product-knowledge` checks: no stack term, plan task or code path, one glossary, a register of open items.

root.description: The folder of the product knowledge.

specification.description: The folder of the product specification, which holds the glossary, the register and the backlog.

glossary.description: The file name of the glossary inside the specification folder.

register.description: The file name of the register of open items inside the specification folder.

backlog.description: The file name of the backlog inside the specification folder.

backlogSection.description: The section number of the backlog, by which a line may point to it (`§<n>`).

excluded.description: Globs, relative to the product-knowledge folder, of files that are not scanned for stack terms, plan references and code paths (history, the register, the backlog).

allowedTerms.description: A file (relative to the product-knowledge folder) and the stack terms that are part of the product there.

implementationPattern.description: A regular expression of the project's code paths and test files, which the product knowledge must not name.

release.description: What `harness release` changes on a release branch.

versionFiles.description: The JSON files whose `version` the release sets; the first one holds the current version.

migrations.description: The folder of the migration notes, one `<version>.md` for every version, with an `areas.json` next to them. `harness release` refuses a version without its note, writes the areas the version touched into it, and links it from the changelog.

lockCommand.description: A command that brings the dependency lock file up to date with the new versions.
